questions.q: Name the literary movement associated with Jaishankar Prasad and identify its one defining characteristic that distinguishes it from Chhayavad.
questions.a: Jaishankar Prasad is associated with Nayi Kavita (New Poetry), specifically the Prayogvad (Experimentalism) strand. Its defining distinction from Chhayavad is the rejection of romantic idealism and musicality in favour of intellectual rigour, colloquial language, and engagement with contemporary social reality. A wrong answer (e.g., "Chhayavad" or "Pragativad") reveals the student conflates literary generations — they have not internalised the chronological and ideological break that 1950s poets made with the past.

questions.q: Explain in your own words why a poet born in 1927 would write a poem titled "कविता के गुस्से" (Poetry's Anger/Playfulness) in the 1950s, linking it to the shift from Chhayavad to Nayi Kavita.
questions.a: A poet born in 1927 came of age after independence, witnessing the disillusionment with Nehruvian ideals and the gap between poetic tradition and lived reality. "कविता के गुस्से" uses "गुस्सा" (anger/playful defiance) to signal poetry's rebellion against inherited forms — just as the new nation had to redefine itself. The poem treats poetry as a child playing in houses (stanzas), breaking rules, because the old "houses" of Chhayavad no longer fit. A wrong answer that treats "गुस्सा" as mere literal anger or misses the generational rupture shows the student reads the title at face value without historical imagination.

questions.q: Given the lines "कविता, एक मकान है फफूंदी का / कविता, एक खेल है बच्चों का" (Poetry is a house of fungus / Poetry is a child's game) from the first poem, apply the concept of "defamiliarisation" (Shklovsky) to explain how the poet makes the familiar concept of poetry strange.
questions.a: Step 1: Identify the familiar concept — poetry as elevated, serious, sacred. Step 2: Note the two metaphors — "फफूंदी का मकान" (house of fungus/decay) and "बच्चों का खेल" (child's game). Step 3: Analyse the effect — fungus suggests something organic, uncontrolled, growing in neglect; child's game suggests rule-breaking, spontaneity, lack of reverence. Step 4: Conclude — by comparing poetry to decay and play, the poet strips it of institutional dignity, forcing the reader to re-perceive poetry as living, messy, and subversive. A wrong answer that only paraphrases the metaphors without naming the *mechanism* (defamiliarisation) or its *purpose* (breaking Chhayavad's sacralisation of poetry) shows surface-level reading.

questions.q: Compare the treatment of "language" in the two poems: "कविता के गुस्से" (where words are playthings) and "बात लह/ख थी" (where language fails to capture experience). What does this contrast reveal about the Nayi Kavita poet's relationship with language?
questions.a: In "कविता के गुस्से", language is material to mould — "शब्दों का खेल" — the poet celebrates linguistic freedom, mixing registers (folk, Sanskrit, Urdu, English). In "बात लह/ख थी", language is a trap — "हकक जककनरह स" (stammering) — the speaker struggles to articulate a transformative experience, and when words finally come, they distort it ("बात बन गई"). The contrast reveals the Nayi Kavita poet's *dual anxiety*: language is both the only tool for new expression and an inherited structure that resists the new. A wrong answer that treats both poems as simply "about language" without analysing the *shift from play to failure* misses the dialectic at the heart of experimental poetry.

questions.q: Evaluate the claim: "Jaishankar Prasad's 'बात लह/ख थी' is a poem about the impossibility of communication." Support your judgement with two textual reasons.
questions.a: The claim is *partially true but incomplete*. Reason 1: The poem *does* dramatise failure — "मैं कुछ नहीं कह सका" (I could say nothing), the listener's "लककनरह" (stammering) reply, the final distortion "बात बन गई" (the talk became something else). Reason 2: However, the poem *enacts* communication through its very existence — the poet *did* find words to record the failure, using metaphor ("हकक जककनरह स", "सपकक स") to convey the inexpressible. Thus, the poem proves communication is *difficult*, not *impossible* — it is a crafted artefact bridging the gap. A wrong answer that agrees wholly ("yes, it's about impossibility") ignores the poem's meta-communicative success; one that disagrees wholly ("no, they communicate") ignores the central tension. The nuanced evaluation is the mark of analytical maturity.

questions.q: Write a four-line poem in Hindi (or Hinglish) that imitates the "child's game" spirit of "कविता के गुस्से" — treating a serious subject (exams, climate change, family pressure) as playful rule-breaking with words.
questions.a: A strong answer will: (a) choose a serious subject, (b) use deliberate linguistic play — mixing registers, breaking syntax, inventing compounds, (c) show awareness that the *form* enacts the rebellion. Example: "बोर्ड परीक्षा / एक पहेली है / जिसका उत्तर / कोई नहीं जानता / गुरुजी भी नहीं / हम भी नहीं / फिर भी / हम खेलते हैं / कलम से / पकड़म-पकड़ाई।" A poor answer writes a conventional moralistic poem ("परीक्षा कठिन है, मेहनत करो") — revealing the student has not internalised that *form is argument* in experimental poetry.
